record.tranche_reason: It evaluates GCG-style adversarial suffix attacks using attack success rate, alongside MAC, on Vicuna and Mistral models. This directly tests whether suffix attacks can bypass refusal, though the paper's main contribution is a momentum variant.
record.gate_note: Only V4 is tested, through adversarial suffix attacks. The paper measures attack success using the presence of refusal keywords, not a separate verification that completions provide harmful instructions. It does not test fine-tuning, first-token KL concentration, compliant prefill, decoding changes, safety-localizing weight edits, causes of shallowness, or deepening safety training.
record.test_reason: An attack-method paper whose ASR tables still report how often optimized adversarial suffixes bypass refusal on two aligned 7B chat models, against a no-attack baseline (Table IV). That bears on V4's suffix clause. Success is judged only by refusal keywords, with a 20-step budget.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim MAC needs fewer optimization steps, and frame it as an efficient white-box red-teaming tool, tested on only two models.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes adversarial suffixes with GCG and a momentum-based MAC variant; it does not use the fine-tuning or token-depth measurement procedures of the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with momentum value, individual versus multiple-prompt setting, model, transfer evaluation, and defense condition.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (2024)
record.problems: Attack success is assessed using refusal-keyword detection, which the authors acknowledge may produce false positives or false negatives. The study tests only two models. Transfer-table layout in the supplied text does not make the suffix source assignment clear. Uncertainty is not stated for the transfer and defense tables.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing V1–V3 or V5–V7 were reported. Individual-attack average-step results and optimization-efficiency comparisons were left out because they do not measure the refusal behavior named by V4.

untested.parts: Compliant-prefill attacks, decoding changes, and a harmfulness check of completions; also the link of suffix success to first-token depth

record.verdict_notes: The record's Table IV reading was wrong. Column-wise, the no-attack baseline is Vicuna 3.0 and Mistral 42.5, and this is the only reading consistent with the text's claim that MAC transfers better for both. Success means the absence of refusal keywords, which the authors call controversial; no harmfulness verification. Vicuna is a lightly safety-tuned model and Mistral-7B barely refuses, so these are weak tests of bypassing strong safety alignment. The paper is primarily about attack efficiency.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning are not tested.
Benign-data fine-tuning and harmful compliance after fine-tuning are not tested.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is not measured.
Adversarial suffix attacks are tested. Compliant-token prefilling, other suffix types, and decoding changes are not tested.
No weights or ranks are localized or edited.
The causes of safety shallowness are not tested.
No training to deepen safety, or evaluation of its durability, is tested.

labels.reason: Table III reports Vicuna average ASRs 35.9-48.6; Table IV reports transfer onto Vicuna at 11.3-12.3 versus 3.0. These show incomplete bypass. Section IV.C explicitly describes aggregation across five folds but does not clearly define the claimed averaging across training steps.

labels.condition: Vicuna with PPL filter or ICD defenses
labels.reason: r39 and r43 show GCG falling from 72.7 to 28.0 and 35.8; r40 and r44 show MAC retaining 76.0 and 62.5. The qualification depends on both defense and attack method.

relation.reason: Its own ASR results and no-attack controls bear directly on V4's adversarial-suffix clause.

tranche.reason: Reports refusal bypass in new suffix-optimization, model, transfer and defense settings, rather than reproducing the original token-depth or fine-tuning procedures.

source_check.notes: ASR uses refusal-keyword detection, not substantive harmfulness grading; experiments use 100 AdvBench prompts and 20 optimization epochs. Section IV.E specifies MAC momentum 0.5, whereas its no-defense 86.1 matches Table III's momentum-0.6 maximum; the text does not resolve this.
